title: Finite-cover sites with finite limits have enough points
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] in the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Assume that its underlying category has finite limits and every covering family of $\mathcal C$ has a refinement that is a finite covering family. Write $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ for its topos of sheaves of sets. Then there is a set-indexed family of points $p_i:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$, where a point means a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism], whose inverse-image functors $p_i^{-1}$ jointly reflect isomorphisms: for every morphism $a:F\to G$ of sheaves of sets, if all $p_i^{-1}a$ are bijections then $a$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00YQ, Proposition proposition-criterion-points (finite limits and finite refinement imply enough points); conservative family in Definition definition-enough-points.

proof.text: For any sheaf F and unequal sections s,s' in F(W), apply lem-trf-point-system-countable-saturation. It produces a small directed poset system U retaining their unequal section germs and lifting every finite covering in its Hom colimits. The comparison between the Hom-colimit expression and inverseSystemHomFunctor is obtained by evaluating the colimit of representables and removing the harmless ULift. Naturality is checked on the colimit coprojections.

source.place: Tags 00YP and 00YQ: iterate the all-at-once refinement countably often to close the finite-cover lifting condition under new germs.

proof.text: For an arbitrary covering indexed by a Type u set, lift its index into Type(max u v) and apply the finite-refinement hypothesis. Reindex the finite refining family by Fin n. The finite lifting property supplies a lift through one refining member; compose with its map to the corresponding original member. Thus inverseSystemSitePoint applies and gives a geometric morphism p with inverse image naturally isomorphic to the section-colimit functor. For the distinguished arrow a:U_i->W, apply the sheafification unit to a to obtain a section of the sheafified representable at U_i, then its colimit class t. Transport t to p^{-1}(h_W^#). Naturality and the sheafification adjunction identify the images of the section morphisms at this element with the retained germs of s and s'. Hence every unequal pair of sections is separated by some point.

proof.text: Make the family small without indexing over all sheaves or all inverse systems. Put A_W=h_W^#. These objects form a separating family by the sheafification adjunction and Yoneda, so Mathlib's wellPowered_of_isDetecting makes Subobject(A_W) small in Type(max u w). For each subobject E of A_W, form Q_E=A_W coproduct_E A_W with its two maps a_E,b_E:A_W->Q_E. Retain the pairs whose corresponding sections differ, and choose a point and an element separating that pair by the previous step. This is a family indexed in Type(max u w). Given unequal sections of any F(W), let f,g:A_W->F be their section morphisms and E their equalizer subobject. The pushout has a map Q_E->F whose composites with a_E,b_E are f,g, so a_E,b_E correspond to unequal sections. The selected point for this E separates them. If its two images under f,g were equal, left exactness would put its chosen element in the image of the equalizer, on which a_E=b_E, a contradiction. Thus the selected small family separates every unequal section pair. Apply point_family_conservative and the equivalence between bijectivity and isomorphy in Type to conclude.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q67-982ece7d2 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item and all four new nodes against Stacks sites.tex: definition-point, 00YA, 00YC, 00YK, lemma-exactness-stalks, 00YM, the introduction to section-criterion-points, 00YO, 00YP and 00YQ. The item's statement matches 00YQ plus 00YK hypothesis by hypothesis and is not weakened; this node has no base-change morphism or coefficient category, and only Stacks is cited. The route stays in unit sk-i-curve-zero, so no tool_uses are needed. Three repairable faults, all fixed. (1) Step 1 had a gap (D4/E5): its 'transfinite chain' of one-cover (00YO) refinements never fixed the number of stages, yet it claimed every element of the final u is handled at a later stage. The gap is real because 00YP lifts only elements of the original u', while 00YQ needs lifting for the refined u. I rewrote Step 1 as a countable iteration: I_{n+1} is the 00YP refinement of I_n and I is their union. Distinctness holds because equality in a directed colimit is witnessed at one index; lifting holds because f in u(W) comes from some u_n(W) and is lifted in u_{n+1}. Step 1 now cites only lem-trf-point-system-refine-all, and I drop lem-trf-point-system-refine, which has no other citer. Step 3 now names x = class of id_U at index 0, so [U,x,s] is the image of s. (2) In lem-trf-point-family-conservative, 'the site functor underlying p_i' was undefined (B2); it is now u_i(U) = p_i^{-1}(h_U^#), citing def-weil-pbc-sheafification. (3) The lifting clause of lem-trf-point-system-refine-all was loose; it now says the image of f lies in the image of u(W_k) -> u(W). I also removed the unused def-weil-size-convention stmt_dep from both nodes. Step 2 checks out: finite limits commute with directed colimits, and composing the lift with W_k -> W_{a(k)} handles an arbitrary covering. Step 3's size argument is valid under the U-in-V convention. lem-trf-inverse-system-site-point is true and is not a duplicate of lem-trf-site-point-reconstruction-sets or lem-trf-site-point-fibre, which start from a given point. reviewed_lean.note: Read node, 3 stmt_deps, IsSiteForCoverings and GeometricMorphism, and Stacks 00YO/00YP/00YQ. Hypotheses (small site, HasFiniteLimits, finite covering refinement with correct orientation, empty I/K allowed; the extra universe v is harmless) and the conservative conclusion match the node. Fault: sheaf values and point index in Type w, independent of the site universe u, making the statement false for w<u. Counterexample u=w+1: meet-semilattice with top, bottom and an antichain indexed by Type w, coverings = families containing an iso (trivial topology); a left-exact inverse image separates bottom from at most one antichain element, so a conservative family would inject Type w into iota:Type w. Fixed to Type (max u w), the faithful Stacks reading (site is a set, values in all sets); unchanged for w>=u. Docstring rewritten to carry node Steps 1-3, with Step 3 indexing points by inverse systems in C, not tuples of sheaves. Note for the lead: the node's proof Step 3 (V-small site, U-valued sheaves, index over all sheaves) should be reworded at stage 3; the statement field is fine. Delivered and fixed modules compile clean with nt_compile.py (3.7 s / 6.1 s). Fixes: FinitarySiteEnoughPoints.lean, lean-record.json (note), report.md (Maintainer fix section).

lean.statement: theorem finitarySite_enoughPoints {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [HasFiniteLimits C] (J : Precoverage C) (hJ : J.IsSiteForCoverings) (hfinite : ∀ (X : C) (I : Type (max u v)) (U : I → C) (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ X), Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ J X → ∃ (K : Type (max u v)) (_ : Finite K) (V : K → C) (g : ∀ k, V k ⟶ X) (r : K → I), Presieve.ofArrows V g ∈ J X ∧ ∀ k, ∃ (q : V k ⟶ U (r k)), q ≫ f (r k) = g k) : ∃ (ι : Type (max u w)) (p : ι → GeometricMorphism (Type (max u w)) (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (Type (max u w)))), ∀ {F G : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (Type (max u w))} (a : F ⟶ G), (∀ i, Function.Bijective ((p i).inverse.map a)) → IsIso a
lean.note: Sheaf values and the point index are in Type (max u w), at least the site universe u (Stacks: the site is a set, sheaves are valued in all sets). The delivered Type w admitted w < u, where the statement is false (presheaves on a meet-semilattice with top, bottom and an antichain indexed by Type w, u = w+1: a left-exact inverse image separating two antichain elements would separate the bottom, so a conservative family needs an injection Type w -> ι : Type w). The universe v of hfinite is harmless: every covering presieve has a Type u presentation and the condition does not depend on the presentation.
